title: NFL Insider reveals Houston Texans did not want to offer Deshaun Watson an extension in 2020
description: Deshaun Watson played his best football with the Houston Texans before his NFL career started going downhill with controversies and injuries. The Texans traded up 13 places to get Watson, who had played college football at Clemson.
fullText:
Deshaun Watson played his best football with the Houston Texans before his NFL career started going downhill with controversies and injuries.

The Texans traded up 13 places to get Watson, who had played college football at Clemson.

It was pure brilliance from Watson from the moment he wore the Texans jersey, with top performances in his rookie season itself.

However, his rookie season was cut short due to an ACL injury, but Watson came back for a massive sophomore season and ended up putting up top performances to make it to three consecutive All-Pro teams.

In 2020, Watson began negotiations with the Texans for his extension. It seemed like that would be the best decision the team could make, as he had proven himself to be a top QB in the league.

However, the franchise had a lot to think about according to an NFL Insider.

Having come off his career-best year, it was certain that Watson was always going to be given the contract he was looking for.

But the Texans had appointed Jack Easterby as their executive vice president of football operations. According to NFL Insider, Tom Pelissero, he was not keen on extending Watson's contract.

"Some on staff didn't want to extend Watson at all—most notably then–executive vice president of football operations Jack Easterby, who had arrived from New England in 2019 with designs on resetting the building and immediately had friction with Watson.

"While often electric on the field, he was frequently late to meetings, wanted increased influence over personnel and coaching decisions, and had trouble correcting some on-field shortcomings, such as a cadence that coaches felt was contributing to pre-snap penalties," wrote Pelissero on his Substack.

The Texans eventually ended up extending him on a four-year, $156 million deal. Watson only played one year before deciding to sit out the next, as he was looking for a trade away from the franchise.

Eventually, a few off-the-field issues came into the open, which ideally should have decreased his value, but the Cleveland Browns decided to give him a chance, and offered him a five-year $230 million deal.

Since then, he has only played 20 games for them and has been the subject of constant criticism from fans and the media.

title: NASCAR Cup Series Driver Steals the Show With Dolly Parton Tribute at Bristol
description: One NASCAR Cup Series driver fully embraced Bristol's Dolly Parton celebration, arriving at driver introductions wearing an unmistakable platinum-blonde wig.
fullText:
Tyler Reddick wasn't exactly difficult to spot during driver introductions Saturday night at Bristol Motor Speedway.

The driver of the No. 45 Toyota emerged in front of the crowd wearing a long, platinum-blonde wig, delivering his own unmistakable salute to Tennessee royalty Dolly Parton.

At a racetrack where subtlety has never exactly been the specialty, Reddick understood the assignment.

The surprise look came as Bristol celebrates Parton during its NASCAR Cup Series weekend, adding another distinctly Tennessee touch to one of the sport's biggest nights of the year.

And Reddick decided to get in on the celebration himself.

Reddick walked onto the driver introductions stage with both arms raised and the blonde wig flowing over his firesuit, leaning all the way into the moment before climbing into his No. 45 SiriusXM Toyota for 500 laps around Bristol's notoriously unforgiving half-mile.

The disguise wasn't going to fool anybody.

Parton's signature blonde hair has been part of her instantly recognizable look for decades, and Reddick's choice made the inspiration clear without saying a word.

The result was one of the more memorable driver entrances of the night.

It was also a fitting tribute at a venue that has spent the weekend celebrating the people and culture surrounding its Tennessee home. Parton's connection to East Tennessee runs far deeper than celebrity alone. Born and raised in the Smoky Mountains, she has built a legacy in the region that extends from music and entertainment to philanthropy.

Reddick's version of a tribute was considerably less formal.

He put on a blonde wig and walked onto the Bristol stage.

Reddick's lighthearted entrance came during a Bristol evening carrying considerably more emotion elsewhere.

The track has also spent the weekend honoring the late Kyle Busch, whose history at Bristol made the venue one of the defining stops of his NASCAR career. Ty Gibbs is driving a special M&M's tribute scheme, while thousands of fans waved yellow towels during Lap 18 of Saturday night's race in Busch's memory.

That made Reddick's Dolly Parton moment a fun change of pace during a night built around celebration, remembrance and plenty of Tennessee personality.

There are easier ways to walk across a driver introductions stage.

But at Bristol, with Dolly Parton being honored?

The blonde wig was tough to beat.

This is the first day I quite literally couldn't stand the heat.

When my family and I arrived on site at Wildcat Stadium for the Benedict College versus Fort Valley State game, it was humid but cloudy. The clouds went away rather quickly, though, and it became unbearably hot, so much so that my family and I decided to go into the student center, where we ultimately began to socialize with alumni and community members. We nearly missed Fort Valley State's comeback and a scoring error that would have likely resulted in the HBCU version of the Michigan-Western Michigan controversy, only for an in-conference matchup.

Benedict College ultimately emerged victorious, 34-33, and the same issues that ultimately have plagued Fort Valley State in the Malon Watson era were showcased. The Wildcats showed tremendous promise against one of the best teams in the conference, and while some things need to change, they showed a level of fight that can carry them through the rest of the season.

Simply put, Fort Valley State's defense was the Wildcats' star. The offense, through most of the first three quarters, simply couldn't move the ball down the field, though there were big plays, such as Roger Payne's 70-yard touchdown run and Don Hudson's 12-yard scamper that ignited the Wildcat comeback. The defense prevented Benedict from putting this game out of reach many times. The Wildcats' defense forced three turnovers from Benedict: one fumble and two interceptions, including an amazing playmaking interception that came off a tackle. The ball then popped into the hands of the Fort Valley State defender, which I saw as a potential turning-point moment for Fort Valley.

We have enough of a sample size of Marlon Watson's Wildcats competing against some of the best teams that the SIAC and Division II football have to offer. The defense has been contending with teams like Delta State, Benedict, and the University of West Alabama, but to truly make that leap to championship level, Fort Valley State has to figure out how to make that offense more competent around Don Hudson Jr.

That was ultimately stuffed by the Benedict College defenders blitzing. That added to the frustration and confusion about what was being called on offense, and whether the offensive line could sustain Don Hudson long enough to make throws in the pocket.

It appeared that Don had happy feet in the pocket, and some of the concepts were odd, even though the short shutdown passes were ultimately successful at several points in the game. While I am a fan of Hudson's ability to play make with his legs and scramble, I think he'll be better served as a true dual threat. To do that, he has to navigate the pocket before bursting out to run.

The touchdown throw to JT Pendleton that ultimately turned into a 61-yard gain before being stopped at Benedict's 6-yard line was a perfect example of the proof of concept of what Dine could be if he used his mobility to navigate in the pocket. He stepped up in the pocket and found Pendleton for a great play and a great game.

Now, granted, Benedict, for some reason, decided to rush only three and play a bit of prevent defense, which ultimately led to that huge gain. Of course, that played a part in how Hudson navigated the pocket. Still, that is proof of concept I want to see more of throughout the season, and for as long as Don Hudson will be at Fort Valley State.

Former Florida A&M Rattler turned Benedict College QB1 Jett Peddy is exactly what the Tigers needed. While Jett had some moments that weren't ideal, he proved adept at calling the game and using both his arms and his legs to make things happen for Benedict's offense. That was a great recruiting win for Ron Dickerson and could be the deciding factor for Benedict ultimately making and winning the SIAC championship and advancing into the NCAA Division II playoffs once again.

I was a fan of how you could see him process the field and decide whether to run or pass in tandem with Benedict's three talented running backs. They put Fort Valley State's defense in precarious situations that, more often than not, Benedict benefited from. It's hard not to say this isn't the best team in the SIAC. I know it's a long season, and Fort Valley gave them all they could handle, but with Petty under center and a stable of talented running backs who can all make plays, Bearded is a team to watch out for.

The game was ultimately defined by a pretty odd scorekeeping error that could have affected both teams' strategy. The game was ultimately defined by a pretty odd scorekeeping error that could have affected both teams' strategy. At the start of the fourth quarter, around the 8-minute mark, Christopher Johnson made a 25-yard rush to the end zone to go up 27-15 after the PAT.

For some reason, the PAT wasn't reflected on the scoreboard, although he made it, so it read 26-15. In a normal game where Benedict goes on to win, the score discrepancy wouldn't have mattered much and probably would have been caught after the game. Because of Fort Valley State's comeback attempt, it became a huge story that left both ESPN+ commentators, Thai Floyd and Sylvester Williams, audibly confused, as well as both teams' coaches. Fans from both Benedict and Fort Valley State were confused, too.

Ultimately, Benedict was assessed the point, and Fort Valley went on to score two touchdowns to tie the game, but instead of going for the PAT, they went for two on the first touchdown to attempt to make it 26-23 because they thought Benedict had 26. The PAT was unsuccessful and ultimately led to what happened at the end. I believe that shows how the incorrect score on the scoreboard affected the game, because if they went for the PAT, the score would've been 27-22.

The touchdown at the end of the game would have made the score 28-27 with Fort Valley in the lead before the PAT. That scenario would have changed the strategy for both Fort Valley State and Benedict, as Benedict would have had to come back on offense, look to the score to regain the lead, and ultimately secure the victory.

While this doesn't take away from Benedict's win, it ultimately is an unfortunate ending to a game that had the opportunity to be one of the games of the year. Nevertheless, Fort Valley State has several things to clean up to ensure this doesn't happen again, especially against better teams in the SIAC and Division II football.

title: Dodgers GM Sends Honest Message on Tarik Skubal Trade
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers sent the baseball world into a frenzy when they traded for Tarik Skubal, but according to Andrew Friedman, it was a move the team was hoping to avoid having to make. The post Dodgers GM Sends Honest Message on Tarik Skubal Trade appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' quest to win their third straight World Series title is alive and well, as they have officially clinched the National League West division with eight games left on their schedule. For now, the team's main goal involves getting healthy, but even if it can't, it should still be the favorite to win it all until further notice.

At the trade deadline, the Dodgers did what they always do and went all-in by acquiring the reigning back-to-back American League Cy Young winner, Tarik Skubal, in a trade with the Detroit Tigers. It was almost expected that L.A. would be the team landing Skubal, but according to general manager Andrew Friedman, this was actually a move the team was hoping to avoid having to make.

With the Tigers failing to sign Skubal to a long-term contract extension over the offseason, he ended up being the big fish that every team wanted at the trade deadline. Of course, landing Skubal was going to require a massive haul of prospects, which is something the Dodgers always seem to have at their disposal.

Los Angeles has developed a reputation for simply being willing to go above and beyond what every other team in the majors is willing to do. Whether it involves shelling out more money for the top free agents, or giving up whatever prospects a team wants for its top player, the Dodgers are always making moves, which is why it wasn't a surprise to see them land Skubal.

Despite that aforementioned narrative continuing to swirl around the team, Los Angeles has claimed that it didn't want to have to make this sort of move this year. According to Friedman, the list of the Dodgers' trade targets started and ended with Skubal, which could help explain why they were so willing to part with several of their top prospects for a guy who is set to hit the free agent market in just a couple of months.

"We looked to do everything we could over the offseason to avoid being a buyer in July, short of a real impact-type talent," Friedman said, per Tom Verducci of Sports Illustrated. "And so, from our standpoint, our buy side list was Tarik Skubal. End of list."

Trading Skubal was always going to be risky for all 29 other teams in the majors because if he hits the open market, the Dodgers are going to be the favorite to sign him. Without a true salary cap in place, nothing is stopping Los Angeles from spending above and beyond what every other team is spending on its roster, and it has put that theory to the test over the past few years.

It's gotten to the point where a lockout feels inevitable, as the Collective Bargaining Agreement will expire at the conclusion of the season, and there has been virtually no momentum towards a new deal. For now, the Dodgers are intent on winning another championship, but their actions could wind up being at the center of a very important discussion this offseason, with many folks viewing the Skubal trade as the final nail in the coffin.

title: UFC 331 live blog: Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski
description: Follow live UFC 331 results for Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski
fullText:
This is the UFC 331 live blog for Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski, the main card light heavyweight bout Saturday at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

Menifield (18-7-1) heads into Saturday night's event as the underdog, but the 205-pound veteran has a habit of spoiling the plans of the matchmakers. This past May, he headed into enemy territory to win a thrilling striking battle against China's Zhang Mingyang, and was previously the first man to defeat French prospect Oumar Sy. He has won three of his past four fights.

The red-hot Baraniewski (9-0) seeks his fourth UFC victory, with none of his octagon appearances lasting longer than 90 seconds. Baraniewski, 27, debuted with a wild win over Ibo Aslan, and followed that up with a 28-second knockout over Austen Lane before scoring another fast finish against Junior Tafa. With a win over the veteran Menifield, Baraniewski likely finds himself with a number next to his name when the rankings are next updated.

Check out the UFC 331 live blog for Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski below.

All aboard the Iwo Baraniewski hype train! Is he the future light heavyweight GOAT or, as Jed Meshew has suggested, just the 205-pound version of Terrance McKinney? We'll learn a lot tonight in this matchup with the always game Alonzo Menifield.

The undefeated Baraniewski is a sizable favorite at -295 according to FanDuel, Menifield the underdog at +240.

Tentative start, both guys respecting each other's power. Menifield lands a right, Baraniewski answers with a left hand. Menifield with a good job, but Baraniewski connects with a power punch and that backs Menifield up. Menifield comes forward and gets rocked again. Baraniewski on the offensive, Menifield wisely ties him up.

They separate and Baraniewski immediately starts throwing, he has Menifield hurt. Baraniewski in top position now, working to get to full mount. Menifield survives but he looks rattled as the round comes to a close, Baraniewski continuing to fire.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Baraniewski.

Menifield immediately comes out swinging and Baraniewski just eats it. No way these guys can keep fighting like this without someone getting flattened. Pace finally slows with the fighters pummeling against the fence. Back at distance, Baraniewski and Menifield looking to establish the jab. Baraniewski connects and immediately goes headhunting, Menifield with good movement to stay out of danger. Neither guy looks particularly fresh right now and there's a lot of fight left.

Gnarly fight inside, Menifield scoring. Whenever he gets going, though, one good counter from Baraniewski gives him pause. Baraniewski beating Menifield to the punch, Menifield's chin is holding up. Menifield with a right across the chin. He ends the round as the aggressor. Close, close round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Menifield. Overall, 19-19.

Before the round starts, they're bringing in a doctor to check on Menifield's hand. All good. The broadcast zooms in and it looks like his thumb is mangled. Eep.

Quick flurry from Menifield and Baraniewski ties him up. He's pressuring Menifield against the fence. Action has slowed to a crawl. This could be good for Baraniewski with his gas tank not exactly at peak capacity right now. Menifield reverses position and now he has fence control. Crowd boos the lack of action. Menifield trying to throw short punches, but Baraniewski stays locked on to him.

We get a separation with about 90 seconds to go. They trade jabs, Menifield with a slight advantage as it looks like he has more energy. The veteran might pull this off. This is a Menifield round for me, but could go Baraniewski's way if he got the first two.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Menifield. Overall, 29-28 Menifield.

Official result: Alonzo Menifield def. Iwo Baraniewski via split decision (29-28 x2, 28-29)

Menifield calls Baraniewski "awesome" and then downplays his thumb injury, saying his problems are nothing compared to that of homeless people. He says his mom used to have to search through trash when he was growing up, "Where I come from, this is my background, I have to be [tough]."

fullText:
Final Eagles injury report ahead of Week 2 game vs. Titans appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

After playing Week 1 with (almost) a fully healthy roster, with only Jonathan Greenard on the injury report after Eli Stowers was placed on IR, things aren't quite so clean for the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2.

On their final injury report of Week 2, the Eagles featured six players but only two with game statuses. Jalen Carter, Hollywood Brown, Cooper DeJean, and Elijah Moore all missed time during the week but are good to go, while Andrew Mukuba is questionable and Greenard remains out as he works back from the summer pectoral injury.

While there were plenty of talking points coming out of Week 1 on offense, from the big passing plays downfield, to the Eagles' deceptive run struggles and rookie Makai Lemon's negative passing yards, on defense, one rose above the rest: Carter injuring his wrist.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Now granted, Carter still played the lion's share of the snaps for Vic Fangio against the Washington Commanders, playing 66 of a possible 70 defensive snaps, but he was seen at practice days later with a cast on his wrist and thus may not be 100 percent in Nashville against the Tennessee Titans.

And yet, even if Carter may be in pain, it hasn't forced him out of action, as he is currently a go to play in Week 2, alongside Brown, DeJean, and Moore, who were limited in some way during practice.

Mukuba also found himself on the injury report during the week, but unlike Carter, he remains questionable for the contest and will likely be a gameday decision for Fangio. If Mukuba, like Greenard, is unable to play in Week 2, the Eagles do have a contingency in place, as they've officially called up rookie safety Maximus Pulley from the practice squad for the game, but it's unlikely the former Wofford Terrier would get much action on defense, considering Fangio's propensity for playing more experienced players more often than not.

On the Titans sideline, Tennessee included three players on their final report of Week 2, with cornerback Cor'Dale Flott questionable with a quad and linebackers Cedric Gray and James Williams questionable with a concussion and elbow, respectively.

Fortunately, while the Eagles have the potential to be without higher-profile players, that shouldn't slow them down too much in Week 2, as their depth held strong against the Commanders and should remain strong, at least against an opponent like the Titans.

Friday’s Injury Report#PHIvsTEN pic.twitter.com/gdkNrruSZ3

— Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 18, 2026

In Week 1, the Eagles opted to roll with a four-man outside linebacker rotation rushing off the edge, largely sticking with their starters in true Fangio fashion, with some supplemental work off the bench from their free agent additions.

Jalyx Hunt led the team with 53 snaps and made a serious impact on the game even if his stats – three tackles – didn't show it. As has become the norm, Hunt can play the pass, the run, or even drop into coverage, and while he didn't get to Jayden Daniels, he was able to force him out of the pocket and take him off schedule. Nolan Smith followed close behind with 47 snaps, holding down the opposite side of the field as a three-down edge rusher, and behind him, the Eagles rotated in Arnold Ebiketie and AJ Epenesa, who had 28 and 12 defensive snaps, respectively.

Would the Eagles like to finish out a game with more than one sack, especially when it came from their back seven? Most certainly, but in Week 1, Cam Ward was sacked three times, and the Titans' offensive line hasn't exactly been considered the best in the NFL, so that problem could fix itself even without Greenard leading the rush.

At safety, however, things get a bit more complicated if Mukuba can't play because the Eagles simply don't have a ton of depth at the position, seemingly by choice.

Against the Commanders, Mukuba was one of only five Eagles players who logged all 70 defensive snaps alongside Zack Baun, Riq Woolen, Quinyon Mitchell, and DeJean. When the Eagles suffered an injury at safety in Week 1, with Marcus Epps leaving the field for a bit to get his shoulder worked on, Fangio turned to Michael Carter II as their sixth defensive back off the bench, logging six snaps.

But if Mukuba can't go? Then the plan may have to be adjusted over a full game, as DeJean does his best work in the slot, not as a base safety. MC2 and DeJean can play the same position and are more or less interchangeable on defense schematically, but when it comes to "true" safeties on the 53-man roster, the Eagles really only have two in Epps and Mukuba after losing Andre' Sam to a season-ending preseason injury against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Against an inexperienced quarterback like Ward, who only completed 19 of his 32 passing attempts in Week 1 against the Jets for 140 yards and a touchdown, being light at safety might not be the worst-case scenario. The Eagles lost Mukuba last year and were able to hold things down with Epps as a veteran option from their practice squad. But against a team like the Chicago Bears in Week 3? Goodness, Fangio can't want to rely on a cobbled-together secondary against a passing game that put up 269 aerial yards in Week 1.

Fortunately, there's still a chance Mukuba could play in Week 2 and that he could be back in time for Week 3 if things are close, but this injury does highlight that, unlike on the edge, the Eagles are rather light at safety and should consider ways to address that heading into the middle of the season and the trade deadline.

Florida State cut the deficit to seven midway through the fourth quarter. Trae'shawn Brown answered with a 20-yard touchdown run with 2:15 remaining, capping a 90-yard drive. Bray Hubbard intercepted Ashton Daniels' pass on the ensuing possession.

Florida State: The Seminoles built an early cushion but could not get enough stops to repeat last season's stunning win over Alabama in Tallahassee.

title: Winners and losers from Florida State’s loss to Alabama
description: Florida State showed flashes offensively, but turnovers, explosive plays, and a road drought that has surpassed 1,000 days defined its loss to Alabama.
fullText:
Florida State had opportunities to change the direction of its season Saturday afternoon. Instead, another road trip ended with a familiar result.

The Seminoles fell 50-36 to No. 10 Alabama Crimson Tide at Bryant-Denny Stadium, dropping to 1-2 after losing consecutive games to SMU and the Crimson Tide. FSU led 21-6 during the second quarter and briefly regained a 28-26 advantage early in the third, but Alabama eventually took control behind 568 yards of offense and a turnover-free performance.

Here are the winners and losers from Florida State's loss in Tuscaloosa, which once again has FSU's fans calling for changes.

Florida State needed more from its passing game entering Saturday, and Duce Robinson answered the call.

Robinson caught six passes for 135 yards and a touchdown, easily his most productive performance of the season. His 20-yard touchdown opened the scoring and helped FSU build an early advantage against one of the best defenses it has faced.

Ashton Daniels also threw for 377 yards, while Micahi Danzy added 89 receiving yards and Jayvan Boggs finished with 69. The Seminoles finally generated the explosive passing plays that were largely absent through the first two games.

The most troubling streak surrounding Mike Norvell's program continues. Florida State has not won a true road game since defeating the Florida Gators 24-15 in Gainesville on Nov. 25, 2023. Saturday marked 1,029 days since that victory.

The Seminoles went winless on the road during both the 2024 and 2025 seasons, and their first opportunity of 2026 produced another defeat. That issue will not disappear anytime soon. FSU still has road games remaining against Louisville, Miami, Boston College, and Pitt.

Florida State accumulated 471 total yards and averaged 7.5 yards per play. Those are numbers that usually give a team a chance to win.

Three interceptions from Daniels made that much more difficult. Alabama finished without a turnover, giving the Crimson Tide a plus-three advantage in one of the game's most consequential categories. Daniels' final interception came with FSU attempting to make one last push inside the final two minutes.

Even with the passing game taking a significant step forward, Ousmane Kromah continued to provide Florida State with production out of the backfield. The sophomore rushed 17 times for 80 yards and a touchdown, including a 12-yard score that gave FSU a 14-3 first-quarter lead.

Kromah has now been Florida State's leading rusher in each of its first three games and continues to look like the most dependable piece of the Seminoles' offense.

Florida State's defensive issues did not disappear during the bye week.

Alabama accumulated 568 total yards while averaging 8.6 yards per play, with quarterback Keelon Russell completing 23 of 30 passes for 320 yards and three touchdowns. He also delivered one of the game's defining plays with a 57-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter.

FSU surrendered 50 points despite forcing Alabama into just three conversions on nine third-down attempts. The Crimson Tide repeatedly found explosive plays before third down could become a factor.

The recent history between these programs gave Saturday's matchup additional weight.

Florida State stunned then-No. 8 Alabama 31-17 in Tallahassee to open the 2025 season, scoring 24 consecutive points in one of the Seminoles' biggest victories of the year. Alabama returned the favor Saturday with 50 points on its home field.

There is also an unavoidable connection to 2023. Florida State finished that regular season 13-0 but was left out of the four-team College Football Playoff, with one-loss Alabama receiving the No. 4 seed while FSU finished No. 5 in the committee's final ranking.

title: Rutgers Stays Close With USC But Loses 44th Straight Against Top 25 Team
description: On Saturday, Rutgers lost 42-35 to No. 12 USC, falling to 0-3 and extending its losing streak against AP top 25 opponents to 44 games.
fullText:
During an on-field ceremony at the end of the first quarter Saturday afternoon, Rutgers honored several members of its team from 2006. Back then, the Scarlet Knights went 11-2, tying the school-record for victories in a season, and finished No. 12 in the final Associated Press poll, the highest year-end ranking in program history. Not much has gone right in the 20 years since, especially since Rutgers joined the Big Ten Conference in 2014.

On Saturday, the Scarlet Knights lost 42-35 to No. 12 USC, falling to 0-3 and extending their losing streak against AP top 25 opponents to 44 games. The Scarlet Knights haven't defeated a ranked opponent since Nov. 12, 2009 when coach Greg Schiano helped them upset No. 23 South Florida 31-0 at home on a Thursday night.

Since Schiano returned in December 2019, Rutgers is 0-16 against ranked teams, losing by an average of 25.4 points. The seven-point deficit Saturday was tied for the smallest against a ranked opponent during Schiano's second tenure, while the 35 points were the most Rutgers has scored against a top 25 team during that stretch. Still, it was of little solace.

"I'm very disappointed for our players and our coaches and our fans," Schiano said. "There are no moral victories. I don't want to hear about that. That doesn't apply. I fully expected to win this game."

Schiano was in the minority. Through Rutgers' first two games, the Scarlet Knights struggled against weak competition. Rutgers opened with a 37-21 home loss against lowly UMass, the Minutemen's first victory in 16 games. The Scarlet Knights then lost 28-21 at Boston College, as quarterback AJ Surace threw four interceptions.

On Saturday, though, the Scarlet Knights hung with a USC team that started 2-0 and has several players who should play in the NFL in the next couple of years. Rutgers finished with 460 yards of offense, just four fewer than USC, and had more yards (289) in the second half than the Trojans (212). Antwan Raymond ran for 122 yards on 21 carries, while receiver KJ Duff had seven catches for 86 yards and made a one-handed touchdown catch late in the first quarter.

Rutgers quarterback Dylan Lonergan, who missed the BC game with an injury, returned and completed 18 of 36 passes for 252 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions. After throwing an interception on his first attempt, he regrouped and made some clutch plays, as did his team, which converted three of four fourth downs.

Trailing 17-7 and facing a 4th and 21 on its own 16-yard line late in the first half, Rutgers converted a fake punt, with punter Jakob Anderson completing a 40-yard pass to defensive back Jesse Ofurie, who was wide open in the middle of the field. Five plays later, Lonergan threw a 16-yard touchdown pass to Elias Coke for 17-14 USC with 1:25 left.

"My decisions tonight are based on who you're playing, (12th-ranked team) in the country," Schiano said. "They have one of the more talented rosters. The pro people I talk to…they have top five talent in the country on that team. You have to take some chances."

Still, Lonergan made some mistakes, as well, including early in the third quarter when Rutgers trailed 20-14 and had a first and goal on the USC 9-yard line. USC safety Prophet Brown stepped in front of Lonergan's pass, made the interception and returned the ball 99 yards for a touchdown, expand the Trojans' lead to 27-14. But Rutgers responded with a three-play, 75-yard drive, culminating in Clay Thevenin's 17-yard touchdown run to cut its deficit to 27-21.

In the fourth quarter, Schiano went for it again on fourth and 1 from the Rutgers 24-yard line. Running back Antwan Raymond received the direct snap, but he couldn't get the first down. USC quarterback Jordan Maiava then threw a two-yard touchdown pass (his second of the night) for a 42-28 lead with 8.41 left. Lonergan followed up by tossing a 28-yard touchdown on fourth and 10 to cut the Rutgers deficit to 42-35 with 4:24 remaining. But USC ran out the clock, keeping its perfect record intact and setting up a major Big Ten home game next Saturday against No. 21 Oregon.

Rutgers, meanwhile, again fell short against a ranked team, calling into question Schiano's future with the program. After coaching Rutgers from 2001 through 2011, the best years in program history, Schiano became the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' head coach, lasting two seasons. He later was an assistant at Ohio State before returning to Rutgers in 2019 to great fanfare.

Still, since Schiano took over for a second time, Rutgers has gone 31-44, including 15-40 in the Big Ten. Rutgers should be a heavy favorite on Friday night against Howard, a Football Championship Subdivision team. But a week later the Scarlet Knights host No. 4 Indiana, the reigning national champion. They also face No. 19 Michigan and No. 14 Penn State, along with five other conference opponents. They can't overlook any of those teams.

After Rutgers went 7-6 in 2023 and won the Pinstripe Bowl, Schiano signed a contract extension through the 2029 season. He is making $6.75 million this year and is owed $22.5 million over the final three years of his contract, per CBS Sports. Those are numbers that are surely on the mind of athletics director Keli Zinn, who came from LSU and started in July 2025.

The schedule presents opportunities for Schiano to defeat Big Ten opponents and show he's the right man for the role. Still, the clock is ticking. And despite praising his team Saturday for hanging in with a ranked team, Schiano knows where things stand.

"There's nobody to blame but me," Schiano said. "I have to figure out how to do it as the head coach. After 39 years of doing this, I have to figure out how to get us over the hump because we're not a bad football team. We're just not quite where we need to be right now."

Join your fellow fight fans tonight!

Brave and stubborn performance from Jimenez, who withstood all sorts of punishment to make it as much of a fight as he could of it. Unfortunately, you don't win rounds with tough guy points. Blancas pasted him from pillar to post from the opening round until the ultimately ending in Round 7.

Referee steps in in the seventh as as he finally sees enough.

Six rounds in and Jimenez is hanging tough but losing every round clean and clear.

Blancas putting a beating on Jimenez, particularly to the body over three rounds. Jimenez has very little to offer by way of resistance.

Ridiculous mismatch of a fight. Fight spills over past the bell in the first.

One-sided beatdown by Verde, with Hernandez's only moment of success coming from a highly questionable knockdown call in the third round. That moment aside, he got absolutely throttled by Verde who hit him with literally every punch in the training manual.

Referee has seen enough, stops it in the fifth.

Doctor evaluating Hernandez to start the fifth.

Four rounds in, Hernandez has won maybe 1% of the entire fight, yet he's the one with the official knockdown. He's otherwise taking a shellacking.

Replay seems to show the knockdown was really a case of a balance shot while Hernandez stepped on Verde's foot. Knockdown won't be overruled, though.

Verde landing everything and the kitchen sink in the third, Hernandez with a high threshold for punishment. VERDE SOMEHOW GOES DOWN AND SAYS IT WAS A SLIP BUT IT WAS RULED OTHERWISE!

Considerable mismatch in talent and skill. Verde teeing off and easily having his way after two, and it doesn't much look like Hernandez wants to be in there. Hernandez took the fight on two weeks notice, and it shows.

Marcial clearly came into this fight with a point to prove and showcased his power advantage early. The crowd was definitely pro-Huerta but that wasn't enough for him to withstand the punches Marcial was dishing out. In the third Marcial landed a beautiful counter shot that put Huerta down and unable to beat the count. Nice one for the highlight reel.

FILIPINO POWER!! WHAT A KNOCKOUT!! 🇵🇭#PitbullBravo | Live NOW on DAZN ▪️ pic.twitter.com/6JwiWjTarK

BEAUTIFULLY TIMED COUNTER PUTS HUERTA DOWN AND OUT!

Heavy punching coming from Marcial, Huerta at an obvious power deficit early, and Marcial just steadily applying pressure and picking his spots to strafe the body and head.

Okay, we're officially underway!

Ring walks starting now! Fight will be getting started momentarily.

Streaming: DAZN (subscription required)

Location: Pechanga Arena, San Diego, CA, USA

Isaac "Pitbull" Cruz vs Nestor Bravo, super lightweights, 12 rounds, for Cruz's interim WBC title

Preview: Cruz (28-3-2, 18 KO) looks to stay relevant at 140, basically, as he can't lose this fight and get a good fight next, but if he wins it, yeah, he'll be attractive for plenty of people, and could force a full WBC title fight with the Dalton Smith vs Alberto Puello winner after their fight on October 24. He could also be lined up to face WBA champ Gary Antuanne Russell. But he has to win here. He's expected to, but Bravo (24-1, 17 KO) does have advantages in height and reach, and they're significant. It's going to come down to whether he can utilize those or not, because Pitbull fights the same, always. He's tough, he's hard to beat, and he makes you earn it.

Daniel Blancas vs Sergio Jimenez, super middleweights, 10 rounds

Preview: We've got BoxRec rankings of 31 (Blancas) and 208 (Jimenez) here. Blancas is 15-0 (7 KO), a 25-year-old Milwaukee native who scored a decent win over Raul Salomon last time out on May 2, and has been inching along as a pro. Jimenez (17-1-1, 15 KO) is a 39-year-old Mexicali-born fighter who had his pro debut at age 33 in 2021, and went to a six-round draw against a fella who came in with a record of 8-56-2. He's done OK since then, but he's fought at very, very low levels, other than a 10-round loss to Deon Nicholson in 2024. On the sheet, this looks like a pretty wack mismatch propped up by one guy's paper-thin record.

Marco Verde vs Guillermo Hernandez, middleweights, 10 rounds

Preview: Verde (6-0, 3 KO) won a silver medal for Mexico at the 2024 Olympics in Paris, falling short in the final against Asadkhuja Muydinkhujaev of Uzbekistan, who are among the big daddies in modern amateur boxing. Verde represented his country wonderfully, but he hasn't exactly been blowing anyone's doors off since turning pro in May 2025, and it's not like he's been matched aggressively or something. He's beating people handily and clean without debate, but anyone would want to see more for an Olympic silver medalist. But maybe that's just not him. Hernandez (7-0, 4 KO) is a 30-year-old from Calgary nicknamed "The Warrior," which is staggeringly generic. He won three fights in El Salvador, one in Colombia, one in his hometown of Calgary, and two club-level fights in Mexico. These are places where you can pad/build a record pretty easily.

Eumir Marcial vs Omar Huerta, middleweights, 10 rounds

Preview: Marcial (7-0, 4 KO) was once given a bit of hype as a possible Next Great Hope out of the Philippines, but the 30-year-old also hasn't really impressed since turning pro in late 2020. He won bronze at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. He also plays basketball for the Basilan Steel of the MPBL in the Philippines, so he's just like Manny Pacquiao other than all the achievements or accomplishments past that bronze medal. Huerta (15-1-1, 13 KO) is a local, 0-1-1 in his last two, including a shutout loss to Vito Mielnicki Jr last time out in April.

title: Dodgers magic number to clinch a bye to NLDS
description: The Dodgers on Monday beat the Reds to clinch a playoff berth for the 14th season in a row, tying the major league record also held by the Atlanta Braves, who made it to 14 consecutive postseasons from 1991-2005. Los Angeles won again in Cincinnati on Tuesday, which eliminated the Arizona Diamondbacks from National League […]
fullText:
The Dodgers on Monday beat the Reds to clinch a playoff berth for the 14th season in a row, tying the major league record also held by the Atlanta Braves, who made it to 14 consecutive postseasons from 1991-2005.

Los Angeles won again in Cincinnati on Tuesday, which eliminated the Arizona Diamondbacks from National League West contention. Then the Dodgers beat the Reds on Thursday, clinching their fifth consecutive division title and 13th in the last 14 years.

The two division winners with the best records get a bye directly into the National League Division Series, which means beginning the postseason on Saturday, October 3 instead of in the wild card round on Tuesday, September 29.

through Milwaukee and Atlanta games on September 19

The Dodgers do not have the tiebreaker with either the Brewers or Braves, which means they have to have a better record to gain a higher seed. The Dodgers' magic number to clinch at least the No. 2 seed over Atlanta is five, or put another way the Dodgers need five of 15 outcomes to fall their way in order to finish with a better record than the Braves. Meanwhile, Atlanta needs 11 of 15 outcomes to claim the No. 2 seed.

Getting the No. 1 seed over Milwaukee is a tougher task for the Dodgers, who have a magic number of 11 to finish with the best record in the National League. That means the Dodgers need 11 of 15 outcomes to fall their way to earn the No. 1 seed, while the Brewers need just five of 15 outcomes to have the best NL record for the second year in a row.

title: Clemson rallies to hand UNC their first loss of the season
description: Bill Belichick’s first Clemson experience went well until it didn’t, and now the Heels are 2-1.
fullText:
Sometimes sports can very predictable in really silly ways. Going into halftime of today's game between UNC and Clemson, anybody outside the Tar Heel fanbase probably said that the mojo was on their side and they had a great chance to pull off a needed win in Death Valley to end a horrendous losing streak against the Tigers. For any Carolina fans like myself, however, there was this sinking feeling that the Heels would find a way to choke, and boy did they ever.

Before we get too far down the rabbit hole, let's first address the first half. UNC opened the game by pounding the ball down Clemson's throat, which resulted in taking an early 14-3 lead. Clemson freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds had a difficult time getting going early on mostly because of nerves, but it didn't help that the Heels' defensive line was forcing him to make some iffy decisions. Reynolds would eventually find his footing, though, but Clemson still couldn't find their way into the end zone. UNC went into halftime up 17-6, and it felt like maybe momentum was on Bill Belichick's side.

To start the second half, though, Reynolds & Co. continued to apply pressure against the Heels' defense. The Tigers scored 10 unanswered points in the second half, and after a while it was clear that UNC didn't have much of an answer. On the offensive side of the ball, Clemson's defense clamped down on UNC's potent run game, which means Billy Edwards Jr. had to prove that he could beat them with his arm. That didn't go well, to say the least, but they were eventually able to get into field goal range in the fourth quarter to make the score 20-15. The three points were scored after yet another severe weather delay thanks to lightning in the area.

When Clemson got the ball back, they ran four plays for 68 yards and got into the end zone. The Heels proceeded to turn the ball over on downs, which then led to the Tigers running five plays and getting into the end zone yet again. On UNC's last possession, Edwards tried to be a hero and connect on a desperation Hail Mary, but the pass was intercepted to end the game.

For anybody wondering how UNC could let such a winnable game slip away, look no further than Edwards' sub-par performance. While he was able to escape pressure with his feet, throwing the ball this afternoon was a disaster. He connected just 13 of his 30 passes for 135 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. He threw a number of bad passes to his targets, missed some guys entirely, and overall just looked bad. Ben Hall and Demon June did a great job of trying to carry the offense on their backs, but ultimately you can't beat many Power Four teams with poor quarterback play. Hopefully it was just a bad day that won't repeat itself, but Notre Dame won't make things any easier in a couple of weeks.

As far as the defense goes, it just seemed like Reynolds proved to be a problem for them once he shook off the nerves. While they deserve a lot of credit for what they were able to do earlier in the game, Reynolds picked them apart from the end of the second quarter onward, and it eventually wore them down. Perhaps things would've went better if Melkart Abou Jaoude wasn't injured, but really we'll never know. Credit to Reynolds for saving Dabo Swinney from embarrassment, but this is a loss for the Tar Heels that will sting for quite some time.

Up next for the Tar Heels is a by week next week, and then the week after they will face off against Notre Dame in Kenan Stadium.

title: She has beaten Alex Eala more times than any other player on the WTA Tour this year
description: Alex Eala has earned some huge wins this year on the WTA Tour. The Filipina star, aged 21, claimed her first such victory at the...
fullText:
Alex Eala has earned some huge wins this year on the WTA Tour.

The Filipina star, aged 21, claimed her first such victory at the Berlin Tennis Open earlier in the season, beating current world number one Elena Rybakina in straight sets.

At Wimbledon, Eala dethroned defending champion Iga Swiatek, beating the Pole 7-6, 6-2 to reach the fourth round of a major for the first time.

She put together the best run of her career thus far at the Washington Open, overcoming Elina Svitolina, Naomi Osaka and Jessica Pegula en route to winning her first tour-level title.

But there is one player Eala just has not been able to find an answer for: Iva Jovic.

Jovic and Eala have met each other three times in 2026, with their first career clash coming at the French Open.

There, Jovic defeated Eala fairly comfortably, emerging victorious in straight sets before reaching the first Grand Slam quarterfinal of her career.

Any claims that the loss for Eala could be explained by clay being her weaker surface were put to bed when the two met on grass at Queen's.

In the round of 16 at the Queen's Club Championships, Jovic handed Eala an even heavier defeat, beating her 6-2, 6-2.

Their third and most recent matchup was the best of the bunch, though, and certainly the most competitive.

Doing battle on hard court for the first time, Eala and Jovic fought for three hours inside a buzzing Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Jovic won her fifth consecutive set against Eala by winning the opener 7-5, and looked to be closing in on another straight-sets triumph.

With both players struggling on serve, Eala was better in the baseline exchanges in set two, which she clinched 6-3.

It was not to be for Eala in the end, though, with Jovic taking the decider to reach the fourth round.

Both Eala and Jovic are in with a shout of qualifying for the WTA Finals for the first time in their careers this year.

Eight players make the cut for the WTA Finals, and the eighth spot is held, as of now, by Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, with 4,234 live points to her name.

Jovic moved up three places recently and is now 14th in the race with 2,232 points, while Eala is just behind on 2,181.

There are still two WTA 1000 tournaments left in the 2026 season where Eala and Jovic can pick up big tallies of points: the China Open and the Wuhan Open.

Currently, only US Open champion Rybakina is qualified for the prestigious year-end competition.

title: Bengals TE Mike Gesicki draws Travis Kelce comparison from Zac Taylor

Burrow harped on Gesicki's feel for the passing game.

"He feels space at an elite level, unlike really anybody that I've ever been around," Burrow said. "He sees it like a quarterback."

Gesicki also caught a 2-yard touchdown in the opener and has scored three times over his last six games dating back to last season.

There could be another opening waiting in Houston, as Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid caught five passes for a career-high 130 yards against the Texans in Week 1.

Gesicki's 78-yard opener continued a productive trend for Cincinnati, which is now 3-1 in games when he leads the team in receiving yards.

title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 32 - Don Adams (1970-71)

fullText:
The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history.

To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day.

With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover.

And for today's article, we will continue with the second of 14 who wore the No. 32, Don Adams. After ending his college career at Northwestern, Adams was picked up with the 120th overall selection of the 1970 NBA Draft by the (then) San Diego (now, Houston) Rockets.

The Atlanta, Georgia native played the first 2 seasons of his pro career with San Diego, coming to an end when he was dealt to the Atlanta Hawks in 1971.

During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Adams wore only jersey No. 32 and put up 11.2 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game.

fullText:
Alonzo Menifield pulled off one of the biggest wins of his career at UFC 331 and he did it despite competing with a mangled thumb that was injured in the opening round.

The light heavyweights were quick to throw with power to start the fight but neither of them were landing just yet. Baraniewski welcomed Menifield into the pocket as they were unloading huge punches.

Menifield connected with a slick combination but Baraniewski showed no fear as he kept firing back and he hurt his opponent as they battled against the cage. Menifield landed a solid punch but Baraniewski returned fire and connected with the better strikes as the light heavyweights hit the floor.

With five minutes remaining, the ringside physician paused the action to check on Menifield's left thumb, which looked like it was barely connected to the hand. But Menifield insisted that he wanted to keep going so the fight continued despite effectively competing with a broken thumb.

The slugfest continued with both fighters landing at times, although Menifield seemed to do a big more damage as time ticked away to the final horn. So far this season, Chelsea have looked dangerous in attack, but weak in defence and open in midfield.

As it turns out, no. In the second half we lost all that solidity without gaining back any of our attacking threat. In the end the 3-0 scoreline felt that much worse simply because we'd made it halfway with the scores level.

title: Royals refuse to give in, but can’t overcome the Rays of Pittsburgh
description: They just kept coming back until they didn’t.
fullText:
Noah Cameron didn't have his best stuff tonight, but he held things together and the offense just kept chipping away. Jac Caglianone had his first two hits since injuring his arm/elbow and Nick Loftin had his second career four-hit game. In the end, though, the three players acquired from the Rays during the offseason played key roles as the Pirates defeated KC 6-5.

Noah Cameron finished the night allowing 4 runs in 6 innings while striking out 6 and walking 2. Those are very mediocre numbers and represent one of his worst starts since late July. If you had told Royals fans that was how you interpreted this outing sometime any time in June or July they'd have tried to have you committed. But that's the world we're living in now. The damage was done primarily on two hits, a pair of two-run homers. The first was by Ronny Simon in the bottom of the second, a switch-hitter who hadn't hit a dinger in his first 121 at-bats. But Cameron left him a changeup in the middle, and Ronny didn't miss. Ronny, by the way, was originally signed by the Rays out of the Dominican Republic.

The second home run was hit by tonight's center fielder, Jake Mangum. Mangum came over in a trade alongside Brandon Lowe and Mason Montgomery from the Rays during the offseason. This pitch was a little better, a backfoot slider that didn't quite get to the back foot.

The final blow was, what else, a two-run home run by a former Ray. This time it was the aforementioned Lowe banging one to right center off of Steven Cruz. It was the final blow.

The Royals offense was churning for most of the night, despite facing one of the nastiest pitchers in baseball this season. They got one run back quickly in the top of the third when Carter Jensen broke the Royals' rookie record for home runs in a season.

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video.

Carter now takes aim at the record for home runs by a rookie catcher set by Mike Piazza and Rudy York. He'll only need… 11 more to surpass their total of 35 each. Still, Carter could become the first rookie catcher to lead his team in RBIs since Piazza led the Dodgers in 1993. His 76 leads Salvador Perez by 4 with 7 games left, and the latter only playing part-time.

The Royals answered the Pirates' home in the fourth by scoring two more of their own in the fifth. Bobby Witt Jr. led off with a single and Jac Caglianone, in his first game back following a one-game suspension for injuring his hand after a bad at-bat Thursday, took a walk to bring the tying run to the plate. The Royals successfully performed a double steal to put runners at second and third with no outs for Vinnie Pasquantino. Vinnie, unfortunately, could only manage a routine grounder to first to score Bobby and advance Jac. That brought up Michael Massey.

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video.

Ryan O'Hearn's acrobatic play cost the Royals a baserunner and who knows what else. Nick Loftin followed that with a single of his own, and John Rave flied out to center to end the inning. If Massey had been on first, it doesn't take much imagination to see him going to third on Loftin's single and scoring on a Rave sacrifice fly to tie the game then and there.

Still, by this point, as you can tell from the clip above, the Royals had gotten into the Pirates' bullpen. That would become important when they turned to Camilo Doval in the seventh inning. Bobby led off again; this time he hit a single off of Doval, but Doval chose to sling it in the general direction of first anyway. That allowed Bobby to go to third. Jac Caglianone added his second single of the night, this one to the opposite field, to score Bob and tie the game. Pasquantino singled, and Jac went all the way to third. Massey struck out, but Loftin came through again with his fourth hit of the night to give the Royals the lead. Unfortunately, Vinnie was stranded at third as Rave and Kyle Isbel each made outs to end the inning.

After Lowe's home run in the bottom of the eighth, the final piece of that Rays trade from the previous offseason made his appearance. Mason Montgomery is the Pirates closer, and close he was planning to do. For a moment, it seemed like the never-say-die Royals had one last trick up their sleeves. Jac Caglianone took a tough walk – he reached base four times on the night. Tyler Tolbert ran for Jac and stole second, still with no outs. Salvador Perez was batting for Vinnie because Montgomery is a lefty, Salvy battled but struck out. Maikel Garcia pinch-hit for Massey and flew out softly to right. Up came Nick Loftin, looking to re-tie the game and mark his first career five-hit affair. Sadly, he popped out in foul territory on a terrific sliding grab by Pirates catcher Henry Davis.

The Royals fell to 67-88 on the season. They still haven't won a series in September and have only two chances left. No matter the outcome of tomorrow's game, they will have had a losing road trip. It's been a resounding thud of a final month after those sweet couple of weeks at the end of August. Tomorrow's game is in danger of rain, and with both teams officially eliminated from the playoffs, it's possible the game is canceled and never made up. However, if it is played, Michael Wacha (3.34 ERA, 4.32 SIERA) will pitch for the Royals. As of this writing, the Pirates have not yet announced their starter. The game will start at 12:35 PM Central Time.

description: Jordan Montgomery parties like it’s fall 2023 to send Texas above .500
fullText:
The Texas Rangers scored six runs while the Toronto Blue Jays scored two runs.

At the last possible moments, the Rangers appear to have stumbled upon a winning formula.

Over the last week or so we've been privy to some victories where the Rangers have scored early, forced the opponent's hand by scratching and clawing their way on base before threatening small ball chaos, and utilized a string of heroic turns from unsuspecting pitchers who have provided multiple effective innings when forced into duty.

If that's the key to victory for Texas, they followed the plan to a Texas T tonight. The Rangers indeed scored early when Josh Jung lifted a first inning opposite field solo home run. Not satisfied with just one run, Texas plated two 

Despite having an aching ankle from getting struck by a pitch, Lopez scampered in the score the third run on a Soriano wild pitch.

Those runs felt pivotal for Texas as one out into the second inning Mr. Quality Start Cal Quantrill exited the game with an disquieting injury. I guess carrying the Rangers on his back over the last month or so has finally caught up with the recently-excellent righty. Quantrill had left his previous start with back tightness, but tonight's early exit was listed as right lat tightness, which isn't great news for the Rangers going forward.

It wasn't great news at the time either as the Rangers were suddenly without this summer's most consistent starter in a crucial game. Former playoff hero Jordan Montgomery was pressed into duty and, like many others over the last week or so, he acquitted himself well. Montgomery entered in a 1-0 game and exited after 3 2/3 innings and 51 pitches having not allowed a hit and with Texas up 3-0.

Another 2023 World Series legend followed Montgomery with Nathan Eovaldi coming in to pitch the sixth. After tossing 46 pitches on Wednesday against Boston, Eovaldi was less effective in his inning of work but he worked around a run to help bridge the bullpen to the late innings.

title: Indiana football's Curt Cignetti teaches Nick Marsh a valuable lesson
description: Indiana football's Curt Cignetti teaches Nick Marsh a valuable lesson ahead of Big Ten play:
fullText:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana football receiver Nick Marsh was back in the starting lineup for the No. 4 Hoosiers (3-0) on Saturday in a 38-0 win over Western Kentucky.

The Michigan State transfer had his best game as a Hoosier too.

Marsh nearly matched his production through the first two games with seven catches for 81 yards. He was targeted a team-high 10 times and would've had an even bigger day if quarterback Josh Hoover hadn't over thrown him on a wide-open vertical route down the sideline at the end of the first half.

The breakout performance came after he sat out the first series against Howard last week.

At the time, Indiana football coach Curt Cignetti told reporters he started Shazz Preston over Marsh in hopes of getting the Tulane transfer more reps, but he offered a bit of a different rationale after Saturday night's shutout victory over the Hilltoppers.

"I mean, he didn't start last week, there was a reason," Cignetti said of Marsh. "And then, we didn't really decide until yesterday who would start there."

More: How Indiana football QB Josh Hoover found his way back to Bloomington

That reason may relate to what Cignetti said on his most recent coaches show about Marsh's practice habits.

"Nick's new, and he's still learning," Cignetti said Thursday. "And, you know, we're still trying to, like, work some kinks out, day in, day out, in terms of practice standards."

It's not the first lesson he's learned from Cignetti during his brief time in Bloomington.

Earlier this season, Marsh showed up to IU's first spring practice wearing gold cleats. The fashion choice didn't go over well with Cignetti, who sent Marsh right back to the locker room to change.

"He learned what getting your a-- ripped is all about," Cignetti said at the time. "I don't know if that happened to him very often at Michigan State. That was before practice started. That was a wake-up call."

Cignetti praised Marsh's progress at Big Ten Media Days, and he made mention of the receiver's playmaking skills throughout fall camp. Marsh flashed that skill set on IU's first drive of the season against North Texas with an impressive one-handed touchdown grab.

On Saturday, Marsh showed once again he's taking Cignetti's teachings to heart, and his teammates see it too.

"I think Nick is a guy that's getting more and more comfortable each and every week," Hoover said. "I think Nick's going to have a really big impact. He already has."

title: How much would it cost FSU to fire Mike Norvell?
description: FSU head coach Mike Norvell has one of the biggest buyouts in college football. Here is what it would cost to fire him after the Alabama loss.
fullText:
The FSU Seminoles lost to the Alabama Crimson Tide 50-36 on Saturday in Bryant-Denny Stadium, and their fans are fed up with the team and Mike Norvell.

FSU came out strong and took a 21-6 lead in the second quarter, but could not keep it going as the Crimson Tide battled back and scored 20 unanswered points in the second quarter to take a halftime lead. They wore Tony White's defense down and scored on their final nine drives of the game, something that has FSU's fans ready for a change.

The Seminoles have now lost their last 10 road games under Norvell and their last 11 games overall away from Doak Campbell Stadium. They have not been much better at home, going 8-19 overall and 3-17 in conference play under Norvell since the start of the 2024 season.

Their performance has been well below FSU's standards, but it will be expensive to move on from Norvell. According to Craig Myers of USA TODAY Sports, his buyout is $46.7 million if he is fired before Dec. 1, 2026. That would be the third-biggest in college football history if they decide to make the move, something they may have to do if the losses keep piling up.

The only two bigger buyouts were the $76.8 million the Texas A&M Aggies paid Jimbo Fisher and the $54 million the LSU Tigers paid Brian Kelly. The Seminoles paid Willie Taggart $18 million when they fired him during the 2019 season, setting up the Norvell hire.

It will not be getting any easier for FSU moving forward. While they have the FCS Central Arkansas Bears next week, their three games after that could be against ranked opponents. First, they will host the No. 25 Virginia Cavaliers before playing the Louisville Cardinals and No. 5 Miami Hurricanes on the road.

title: Keyonte George’s extension is just the beginning for the Utah Jazz
description: "I feel like we’re just getting started on building something super exciting," Ryan Smith said Saturday.
fullText:
Sitting on a stage on the practice court of Zions Bank Basketball Campus, Utah Jazz governor Ryan Smith told fans, his players and the media Saturday that the best is yet to come for the franchise, and Keyonte George's new contract extension is part of that.

George signed a five-year extension with the Jazz on Friday, which ESPN's Shams Charania reported is worth $157.5 million. The deal breaks down to $31.5 million annually. George is now committed to the Jazz through the 2031-32 season,

"I feel like we're just getting started on building something super exciting, so this is just another phase in that journey and the best is ahead of us," Smith said.

George is coming off a breakout season in 2025-26, as he set career highs in points (23.6), assists (6.1), rebounds (3.7), and field goal percentage (45.6) in his third campaign in the NBA. Head coach Will Hardy said this is still just the beginning for George.

"I couldn't be more proud of the player that Key is becoming, and I couldn't be more proud of the young man that he's becoming," Hardy said. "I say the word 'becoming' intentionally, because he's nowhere near his potential as a person or a player."

Hardy called George's extension a "moment of pride for our staff," and he said it was an honor to be George's coach.

The 16th pick of the 2023 NBA Draft, George is one of the "wins" throughout the team's rebuild, according to his team owner, who noted the "major shift" within the Jazz that is coming.

"Our best years in Utah are ahead of us, and I think it's pretty clear," Smith said. "Everywhere I go outside this state, people talk about it, they feel the vibe, they know it's coming and we've got a lot going on."

Smith used George going "all in on" the Jazz despite "hard criticism" as an example of the "magic that can be created."

"We hope that it doesn't stop, because to get to where we want to go, which is ultimately holding a trophy and having a parade, it's going to take a lot of people to do that," Smith said.

"I like where we're going. This is a step in the journey, and we're going to see more and more of this and build that continuity."

For George, his extension "still doesn't feel real."

He thanked the front office for getting the deal done and his teammates for their support. The point guard knew he wanted to stay with the Jazz long term.

"Special shoutout to the city. Obviously, I got drafted here. All I know is Utah," he said.

The 22-year-old added that he may have grown up in Dallas, but "another part of my life I'm about to grow up in Utah."

George "had no pushback with anybody" during the extension process, he said.

"This is my second family," he said. "I mean, I feel like Utah's my second family, so signing here, staying here, in my mind, was a no-brainer."

George's embracement of Utah hasn't gone unnoticed by the Jazz either.

"When I think about the last three years with Key, it goes along with the principle that we have at (Smith Entertainment Group) of just being all in," Smith said.

"Key has been absolutely all in on our community. We've all seen that. He's been all in on his teammates, showing up for them, and most importantly, all in on the organization, the coaching staff and especially the relationship with Will."

As a result of George being "all in on his teammates" as Smith put it, his teammates were there Saturday, sitting in the second row to support him. They were also the first people he celebrated with on Friday.

locked in on mountain basketball 🏔️✍️#TakeNote pic.twitter.com/2Dce1jeAkx

"It meant a lot," George said of that celebration. "We all dream for this moment. I was more excited that I was in the gym with all of them. Just being able to, like I said, share that moment with them, because without them I don't get to this point."

If it's up to George, he'll be wearing a Jazz jersey long past 2032 when his contract expires.

"I want to be around," he said. "If it was up to me, I want to be around forever."

fullText:
A free meme generator that runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers:
an in-browser editor for 450+ templates, plus a URL-based API where every meme is just a link.

Every template has a human-facing, SEO-friendly editor page rendered by src/views/editor.ts:

The editor (assets/static/editor.js) runs entirely in the browser, imgflip-style:

Each page is server-rendered with a unique title, meta description, canonical URL, Open
Graph and Twitter Card tags (the example meme is the social image), JSON-LD (WebSite
with SearchAction, WebPage, ImageObject, BreadcrumbList), an <h1>, descriptive
copy, the template's source link, keyword links, and related templates. Without JavaScript
a <noscript> form posts to POST /images instead.

The site name in titles and social cards comes from the SITE_NAME variable.

The site is installable: /manifest.webmanifest (icons generated by
npx tsx scripts/build-icons.ts into assets/static/icons/), a service worker at /sw.js
(assets/static/sw.js, its cache name bound to the asset content hash so every deploy
refreshes caches), and an /offline fallback page. The worker serves pages network-first
with an offline fallback, and caches static assets, fonts, template images, and the last
80 rendered memes cache-first. On phones, assets/static/pwa.js shows a closeable
"Install" banner: Chrome/Android use the native prompt, iOS gets "Share → Add to Home
Screen" instructions; dismissal is remembered for 14 days and the banner never shows once
the app is installed.

Every template page explains what the meme is, where it comes from, its alternate names,
and related tags, so people can find a template by describing it rather than knowing its
name. The search on / (and ?q=) matches names, aliases, keywords, tags, example text,
and the description; multi-word queries require every word to match.

Know Your Meme excerpts are short, attributed, and linked; write original copy in the
manual file when you want fully unique page text.

Requirements: Node 20+, a Cloudflare account for deployment.

Cloudflare's free plan limits Workers to 10 ms of CPU per request, which is not enough
to render images. Deploy on the Workers Paid plan; wrangler.jsonc sets a 30 s CPU limit.

Variables are defined in wrangler.jsonc (vars). Secrets go through wrangler secret put
or a local .dev.vars file (see .dev.vars.example).

title: Comparing reflection capabilities of C++, Zig and C3
description: Comparing reflection capabilities of C++, Zig and C3
fullText:
Reflection lets a program inspect and manipulate its own structure at runtime or compile time. All C++ (with its upcoming reflection support), Zig and C3 rely on compile-time reflection, so you can reason about types, enumerators, and struct members without any runtime cost. In this post I will compare how these languages approach compile-time reflection.

C3 is a relatively new programming language which mainly focuses on readability, performance, minimalism, and familiarity for C/C++ programmers.

 It doesn't have heavy runtime, garbage collection, exceptions or RAII.

 It also fully supports C ABI compatibility out of the box.

C3 uses special syntax for compile-time execution: all variables, control-flow constructs are prefixed with $. This was done on purpose to explicitly show the reader which code runs at compile time.
It uses macros for compile-time evaluation and reflection.

Let’s see all languages in action!

In Zig, the only solution I can think of is attaching a method to each enum you want to turn into a string, not a generic approach.
I’m not a profound zig expert so you can correct me in the comments.

In C3 enums have special properties. For example, if you want to print enum value, it will print it in a readable form, exactly as defined in the source code.
For example, this code: io::printfn(“%s”, Color.RED) will output RED, not 0.

If you want to take the underlying value from an enum, you can either access .ordinal or cast it to the underlying type.

You can also associate values of any type with your enumerators:

Let’s proceed with reflections!

Here, (1) C3 uses optional pre-conditions called 'contracts' which can help drastically with input validation.
They will be executed at compile-time if it is possible, if not - at runtime.

Zig:

Zig unfortunately doesn’t have ‘attributes’ or any substitute to attach compile-time data to struct members.

For this example with C3 I want to show you 2 options. In the first (1) variant we validate everything at compile-time, we can verify this easily by putting @const attribute on the macro.
In the second (2) variant we’re mixing compile-time attributes with validation at runtime. In this example you can see how syntax distinction between $if and if helps to understand
which code gets expanded at compile-time and which will execute at runtime.

All observed languages can do real compile-time reflection, which is great for serializers, debug printers, and generic helpers like the ones above.
The tradeoff is ergonomics: C++ gets the power via verbose template machinery and splices,
 while C3 makes the same ideas more readable and expressive through its macro system and special syntax for compile-time execution,
 it's very easy to understand where code will execute at compile time and where it wouldn't.

Zig in turn doesn't have macros, instead it relies on comptime functions and blocks, inline for loops and type-introspection builtins, which is also a good, modern and mostly readable approach.

Personally, I've found C3 to be a very promising systems programming language that needs more attention; everybody knows about C++ and Zig is marketed very well, but C3 lacks that kind of marketing, though it can compete easily with Zig, Odin, or any other new systems programming language out there.

 Also it doesn't have tons of breaking changes with each minor version. It's a lot more stable than Zig (honestly, it's pretty embarrassing that Zig is still stuck on 0.1x versions after over 10 years of development), and since C3 is already on 0.8.x versions, 1.0 is very close, see the roadmap.

You can search for more info about C3 on the main website.

title: Using system-one models inside high-throughput data pipelines
description: Jev (the system-one model) used with hank-based fallbacks can cut entity resolution costs and time by incredible amounts. Here's how.
fullText:
Jev (TypeSafe's system-one model) is a quantum leap forward for data processing pipelines, if harnessed correctly. We used Jev to accelerate an entity resolution pipeline to join donors and committees across Ohio campaign finance data. Hank-assisted resolution pipelines that use Jev as the workhorse reduced model costs by 99.56% and increased measured call-time throughput to 7.35× the baseline while retaining near-Fable quality.

But it's not all roses. Applying the wrong signal or prompting the wrong way causes large mistakes at scale. No free lunches, only subsidised ones.

We'll talk about the results, explain the task of entity resolution, and at the end we'll provide some prompts and principles that can work for integrating models like Jev into AI data pipelines.

On a segment of the Ohio dataset that we selected to be difficult, using Fable to join entities costs $9.83 for 1.2 MB of prepared evidence, and takes 844.64 seconds.

An optimized hank (like the one below) is an alternative to direct comparisons using a model or a code-based approach. Here, it reduces model costs to $0.3012 for 715.08 seconds (a 32.6× reduction in cost but about the same time).

Using only Jev to adjudicate drops accuracy significantly, but Jev as the primary workhorse inside a five-family review stage with Luna provides 226x lower cost ($0.0000361 per KB), 7.35x higher throughput (10.5 KBps in call-seconds against Fable's 1.4), while being within 0.5 percentage points of Fable in accuracy.

Jev is the final missing piece for something we set out to do 18 months ago; to scale these workflows up to Terabytes of data.

The task is simple. Can we resolve entities across the Ohio Campaign Finance dataset? Entities here could be donors, committees, companies, etc. This is the task we have been working on as part of a much larger ingestion and data pipelining test designed to measure 4a, our internal superagent that can autonomously build and self-optimize AI data pipelines.

In practice, ER is incredibly difficult. Humans make honest mistakes - middle names are a common example.

We also move houses and jobs, change names, get married, omit information, and overall shenaniganize our lives.

Then there's (alleged) hostile obfuscation - large donors and companies attempting to spread out detection with different entity names, honest looking mistakes, etc etc.

Our ER pipeline resolves these problems using atoms - bundles of equivalent donor evidence. We put rows together into atoms, and models decide on what these bundles are (a company, a person, a committee, a joint donor or an unnamed record), and how they're related (same person, same household?). As we join more and more atoms, the dataset slowly resolves itself.

Here's one case: 11 rows, five atoms, two people. Ordinary code makes the atoms and keeps every original row. Jev judges which atoms represent the same donor, then whether the two donors share a household. The household is a connection between people, not permission to merge them.

If you were so inclined (either rich or a frontier lab), you could have a frontier LLM adjudicate every atom and bundle. However - even if you could pay for all of this (our estimate for the four-file Ohio snapshot is about $9,614 for Fable) - speed makes it difficult to do so. Even the best of us only have about 3 billion seconds of life.

Additionally, we have found that at scale, using cheaper models with additional review steps can surpass the accuracy of even frontier models deployed raw.
